BRA.note: USDA FAS Sugar (Nov 2024): Brazil is the world's largest producer and exporter. Centre-South cane crush drives ~34 Mt of raw+refined exports; WITS importer reports confirm Brazil as the dominant single origin for nearly every major buyer in 2024.

IND.note: USDA FAS: India is #2 producer but exports are policy-capped; 2024/25 exports limited to protect domestic supply and ethanol diversion. WITS confirms India as the lead supplier to Sri Lanka and a mid-tier supplier to Malaysia/Saudi.

THA.note: USDA FAS: Thailand is the #2 exporter after Brazil. WITS importer reports show Thailand as the second supplier to Indonesia (982 kt), South Korea (495 kt) and Malaysia (300 kt) in 2024.

GTM.note: USDA FAS: Guatemala is Central America's largest exporter. WITS confirms 266 kt to the USA and 129 kt to Chile in 2024.

AUS.note: USDA FAS: Australia exports ~80% of raw output, heavily to Asia. WITS confirms 695 kt to South Korea and 788 kt to Indonesia in 2024.

MEX.note: USDA FAS: Mexico exports almost exclusively to the USA under USMCA. WITS confirms 446 kt to the USA in 2024.

CHN.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: China imported 4,348 kt under HS 1701 (gross), led by Brazil (3,833 kt). Production ~11 Mt cannot cover ~16 Mt consumption, so China is a structural net importer.

IDN.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: Indonesia imported 5,314 kt (HS 1701, gross) — the largest single-country buyer — mainly Brazil (3,407 kt), Thailand (982 kt) and Australia (788 kt).

USA.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: USA imported 3,484 kt (HS 1701, gross) from a TRQ-allocated set led by Brazil (1,257 kt), Mexico (446 kt) and Guatemala (266 kt).

DZA.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: Algeria imported 1,238 kt (HS 1701, gross), almost entirely raw cane from Brazil (1,237 kt). Algeria refines and re-exports white sugar regionally.

NGA.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: Nigeria-reported imports were 522 kt from Brazil (the only quantity-reported partner). Raw cane is refined domestically by Dangote/BUA; true consumption far exceeds reported import volume.

MYS.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: Malaysia imported 2,390 kt (HS 1701, gross) — Brazil (1,798 kt), Thailand (300 kt), South Africa (181 kt). A raw-sugar refining hub with minimal domestic cane.

EGY.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: Egypt imported 1,014 kt (HS 1701, gross), dominated by Brazil (955 kt). Domestic beet+cane production trails consumption.

SAU.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: Saudi Arabia imported 2,210 kt (HS 1701, gross), 97% raw cane from Brazil (2,143 kt). Refines and re-exports white sugar across the Gulf and East Africa.

KOR.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: South Korea imported 1,655 kt (HS 1701, gross), with Australia (695 kt) and Thailand (495 kt) lead suppliers; no domestic cane.

MAR.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: Morocco imported 2,508 kt (HS 1701, gross), almost entirely raw cane from Brazil (2,504 kt). State refiner Cosumar processes raws; balance is refining/stocks.

LKA.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: Sri Lanka imported 566 kt (HS 1701, gross), led by India (335 kt) and the UAE (90 kt, re-export hub). Negligible domestic cane sugar.

CHL.note: WITS/UN Comtrade 2024: Chile imported 607 kt (HS 1701, gross) from regional suppliers — Argentina (179 kt), Brazil (165 kt), Guatemala (129 kt), Colombia (100 kt). Beet sugar (IANSA) covers the rest.

BGD.note: Bangladesh did not report HS 1701 imports to UN Comtrade for 2024; figure is USDA FAS Sugar estimate (~2.2 Mt raw imports, refined by City/Meghna groups). Carried as modeled pending a reporting year.

rankings.note: Exporter ranking from USDA FAS Sugar 2024/25 raw-value exports; Brazil and Thailand dominate. Importer ranking is WITS/UN Comtrade 2024 reported HS 1701 gross-import quantities, except Bangladesh which is a USDA estimate (non-reporter). EU collectively is a net importer spread across member states, not ranked as one line.

companies.name: Raizen
companies.note: World's largest individual sugarcane processor and a top sugar+ethanol exporter; crushes ~80 Mt cane across its Centre-South mills, feeding the dominant Brazil-origin flows.
companies.improve: Should publish mill-level cane crush and the sugar/ethanol mix split to show how much of Brazil's ~34 Mt export capacity is single-firm.

companies.name: Cosan
companies.note: Brazilian holding controlling Raizen sugar/ethanol plus logistics (Rumo) that move cane sugar to port; key to Brazil's export dominance.
companies.improve: Should link Rumo rail/port throughput to seasonal Santos export volumes for transparency.

companies.name: Mitr Phol
companies.metric: Revenue ≈ US$3.5bn (FY2024); Asia's largest sugar producer
companies.note: Largest sugar producer in Asia and #4 globally; anchors Thailand's exports to Indonesia, Korea and Malaysia.
companies.improve: Should break out Thai vs overseas (China/Australia) cane assets to attribute flows by origin.

companies.name: Sudzucker
companies.note: Europe's largest beet-sugar producer; supplies intra-EU and the smaller beet-sugar flows to Egypt, Sri Lanka and North Africa.
companies.improve: Should split beet-sugar volumes by EU member plant to map the dispersed EU export footprint.

companies.name: Tereos
companies.note: French cooperative, #2 European sugar group with major Brazilian cane assets; bridges EU beet and Brazil cane supply.
companies.improve: Should attribute Brazil-origin volumes to Tereos Acucar Brasil separately from French beet.

companies.name: Wilmar Sugar
companies.metric: Australia's largest raw sugar producer (~2 Mt); part of Wilmar International (~US$67bn group revenue)
companies.note: Owns the bulk of Australian milling capacity (Sucrogen) plus Indian refining; underpins the Australia-to-Korea/Indonesia flows.
companies.improve: Should separate Australian raw-export tonnage from Indian domestic refining to avoid double-counting.

global.note: Global sugar, kt raw value, USDA FAS Sugar: World Markets & Trade. Production rebuilt after the 2023/24 dip on strong Brazil cane; consumption rises steadily on Asia/Africa demand. Exports ~66-68 Mt with Brazil supplying roughly half.
